key_insight: MosaiQC is a scalable heuristic framework for quantum circuit cutting that jointly optimizes wire and gate cuts while supporting mixed-size hardware partitions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path to execute larger quantum algorithms on limited hardware by reducing cutting overhead and improving partition placement quality.
method: Hybrid warm-start plus refinement optimization for cut placement
Supports both wire cuts and gate cuts in one framework
Uses a fast approximate quadratic assignment solver to place hardware partitions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a mean local fidelity improvement of 19.56% ± 6.17%, 2.88× faster runtime, and an average 16.84% cut reduction, corresponding to a 5.83×10^11× overhead reduction.
watch_item: Results are heuristic and approximation-based, so performance may depend on circuit structure, partitioning choices, and solver tuning.
paper_title: MOSAIQC: Mixed-topology-aware Optimization for Scalable Approximate noise-Informed Quantum circuit Cutting
